title: Urban roadside-grass management yields and IFBB/anaerobic-digestion reference observations
citation: Piepenschneider, M., Hensgen, F., & Wachendorf, M. (2016). Biomass yield and energy content of grass from urban roadside verges. In The Multiple Roles of Grassland in the European Bioeconomy, Grassland Science in Europe, Vol. 21, pp. 855–857.
source_locations: Contribution pages 855–857; harvest methods and results pp. 856–857
geography: Ten urban roadside-grass investigation sites in Kassel, Germany
license: Proceedings PDF is publicly accessible; no explicit reuse license for the contribution was identified. Transcribed values are attributed; check reuse terms before external redistribution.
material_scope: Urban roadside grass managed under two-cut IFBB, four-cut anaerobic-digestion, and eight-times-mulching reference regimes in 2013 and 2014. Silage from two- and four-cut material was used for conversion tests.
experimental_conditions: Ten sites were split across the three management options. Yield sampling was triplicate on 0.25 m2 plots cut to 5 cm; sampling intervals were 12 weeks for two-cut, 6 weeks for four-cut and 3 weeks for mulching. Samples were dried at 105 °C for dry-matter estimation. Remaining biomass was ensiled for at least six weeks. IFBB material was mashed with warm water for 15 minutes and mechanically separated with a screw press. The accessible proceedings do not specify water temperature/addition ratio, press settings, methane-test reference conditions or replicate count for methane tests.
data_scope: 19 records: year-specific and two-year mean annual dry-matter yields with reported SD for three management regimes; minimum ensiling period; mashing and screw-press procedure; reported specific methane yields for 4-cut silage, 2-cut silage and 2-cut press fluid; press-cake LHV; and source-calculated gross energy output per hectare for two configurations.
limitations: Reference-only; Kassel urban verges are not Dutch roadside grass and do not provide GreenHub site access, collection, transport or delivered-feed records.
The proceedings do not report per-site raw yield records, sample counts per management treatment, or full seasonal-cut-level yields. SD is retained as printed without an inferred sample count.
Mulched biomass was left on site and is not an annually collectable feed quantity.
Silage values do not report initial-to-final mass recovery, leachate, or component mass balance.
Warm-water mashing and screw-press method are reported, but water temperature/rate, press settings, throughput and electricity are absent.
Specific methane yields are reported without replicate count, variance, exact methane-test reference conditions, or full configuration data; they are not continuous-digester performance parameters.

The conference contribution reports press-fluid methane yield 269 L_N/kg VS; a later related journal article reports a different 292 L_N/kg VS maximum. These values are kept separate and must not be pooled without treatment/test comparison.
Reported gross energy output is a source-calculated gross value, not net energy, TEA, LCA or evidence of economic feasibility. The AD and IFBB values use different management regimes.
The 16 MJ/kg DM press-cake lower heating value is source-calculated from higher heating value using an equation, not a direct calorimeter measurement of LHV.
No reuse license for the proceedings contribution was identified.
conversion_or_processing: Values transcribed from the proceedings text. No unit conversion, imputation, interpolation, reconciliation with later journal values, or runtime activation was performed.
uncertainty: Annual yield SDs are retained as reported. Sample count per treatment is not established by the proceedings excerpt. Methane yields, press-cake LHV, gross energy outputs and process conditions are reported without uncertainty.
